title: Release guardrails checklist and evidence automation playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, practical checklist and automation playbook for production releases that require RBAC v2 validation, audit log schema compliance, and SIEM export evidence. Target audience: release engineers, SREs, security reviewers, and product engineers prepping a go-live. This doc is intentionally operational — meant to be used in shiprooms and as the source for automated evidence collectors.

Scope:
- Applies to any prod-facing release (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) that touches auth, KMS, networking, or observability changes.
- Excludes purely UI-only cosmetic changes (small text updates) unless they touch auth/config.

Quick runbook (90-minute shiproom):
1) Pre-check (owner: release lead) — 20m
   - Confirm RBAC v2 policy bundle is included in the release artifact and references the correct role ids (check artifact tag: rbac-bundle:v?).
   - Verify automated unit/regression tests for role resolution passed in CI (link build).
   - Validate that the release has a linked security ticket (format JIRA-SEC-####) and at least one security reviewer assigned.
   - Ensure the candidate deployment path has SIEM export configured for the target environment (integration key present).
2) Evidence snapshot (owner: SRE) — 25m
   - Run evidence automation job (see CLI below) to collect: active RBAC policies, service principal bindings, KMS access logs for last 7d, audit-log sample (last 30 min), and SIEM ingestion status.
   - Upload evidence bundle to evidence bucket and link to the release ticket.
3) Security sign-off (owner: security reviewer) — 20m
   - Quick review of RBAC diffs, log samples for sensitive operations (key unwraps, grant role changes), SIEM index ingestion success and alerting rules that would be triggered.
   - Approve or request exception. If exception requested, complete the minimal exception template below.
4) Final gating (owner: release manager) — 25m
   - Check that all required artifacts exist and that any exceptions are acknowledged and timeboxed.
   - Toggle release flag to allow rollout.

RBAC v2 checklist (must pass or exception):
- Policy artifact bundle present and versioned
- Role ids documented in release notes and linked to internal role catalog page
- No wildcard principals in production role grants (explicitly deny in policy linter)
- Critical admin roles have 2FA and time-limited sessions configured
- Service accounts used by the release have least-privilege permissions and rotation schedule defined
- Policy change includes automated test coverage for allow/deny behavior
- Changes to builtin roles require CISO notification and separate approval

Audit log schema sanity (quick validator):
- Required fields present in sample: timestamp_ms, request_id, actor_id, actor_type, action, target_id, target_type, outcome, metadata_version
- Ensure metadata_version matches current schema (v3) and deprecation warnings are absent
- For KMS events include: kms_key_id, operation, ciphertext_length, decrypt_outcome
- For RBAC events include: policy_id, changed_fields, previous_version, new_version, approver_id (if applicable)
- No PII in message_text or free-form message fields; any PII must be redacted before SIEM export

SIEM export validation steps:
- Verify the export connector is in healthy state in the target environment dashboard
- Confirm that the last successful push timestamp is within expected window (<= 5m for real-time pipelines, <= 15m for buffered exports)
- Check index mapping: audit.events.* fields are mapped to the canonical schema (use the mapping table below)
- Run sample ingestion: tail the generated audit sample and assert it appears in SIEM index with correct parsed fields
- Confirm alerting rules triggered on forged authentication attempts or role elevation events in a dry-run mode

Mapping table (canonical -> example field name):
- canonical.timestamp_ms -> audit.ts
- canonical.request_id -> audit.rid
- canonical.actor_id -> auth.user.id
- canonical.actor_type -> auth.user.type
- canonical.action -> evt.action
- canonical.target_id -> evt.target.id
- canonical.outcome -> evt.outcome
- canonical.metadata_version -> audit.meta_v

Evidence automation CLI (run during Pre-check / Evidence snapshot):
- Purpose: produce a single tarball with the key artifacts required for sign-off and upload it to the release ticket.
- Example run (team use): 
  ./tools/collect_evidence --release=${RELEASE_TAG} --env=prod --since=7d --output=/tmp/evidence-${RELEASE_TAG}.tgz
- Items produced by the collector (explicit):
  - rbac/policies.json (current bundle)
  - rbac/diff.patch (diff vs prod canonical)
  - logs/audit-sample.jsonl (last 30m)
  - logs/kms-activities.jsonl (last 7d filtered)
  - siem/ingest-status.txt (connector health + last_push)
  - meta/collector-manifest.txt (collector version, args, checksum)
- Upload process: evidence uploaded to gs://redwood-evidence/${RELEASE_TAG}/ and link posted to ticket; encryption with CMEK is required.

Exception approval template (use when a hard blocker exists):
- Short reason: one-line summary
- Impact: features/users/components affected
- Compensating controls: temporary monitoring, reduced blast radius, manual approvals
- Duration: exact expiry date/time and rollback plan if not remediated
- Required approvers: security reviewer, SRE lead, product owner (names + signature in ticket)
- Evidence to include: targeted audit sample, mitigation config, runbook for emergency rollback

Sign-off matrix (who signs what):
- RBAC policy changes that affect admin/infra roles -> security lead + SRE director
- KMS/key rotation changes -> security lead + crypto owner + ops lead
- SIEM pipeline changes or mapping updates -> observability owner + security analyst
- Any exception -> CISO delegate or head of platform

Common failure modes and immediate mitigations:
- SIEM connector lagging: revert mapping change, route to alternate buffer index, and re-ingest backlog
- RBAC regression in staging tests: rollback policy bundle, block release, notify on-call
- Missing audit fields: block export, auto-attach schema validation job to pipeline and escalate to infra on-call

How to document sign-off in the release ticket (template):
- Checklist: RBAC bundle present [YES], Audit schema sample [YES], SIEM ingestion [YES], Evidence uploaded [GS_LINK], Exception approved [NO]
- Signatures (post message): Security Reviewer: Priya Rao (timestamp), SRE Reviewer: Diego Martinez (timestamp), Release Manager: Ava Chen (timestamp)

Appendix A — Minimal evidence checklist (for a quick triage):
- rbac/policies.json (<= 2MB snippet)
- logs/audit-sample.jsonl (<= 500 lines covering role change and API key usage)
- siem/ingest-status.txt (within last 5 min)
- meta/collector-manifest.txt (collector version and args)

Appendix B — Helpful links and search queries:
- Confluence: Security release playbooks (CONFLUENCE-1234)
- Jira: security intake board (filter: project = SEC and status in (Open, In Review))
- SIEM: index audit.events, query: evt.action: ("grant_role" OR "kms.decrypt") AND evt.outcome:failure
- GitHub PR: security-playbooks repo (PRs tagged with release/${RELEASE_TAG})

Notes and open questions:
- Should the collector default to a 14d KMS export window for high-risk releases? (open, tagging: security-decision)
- Do we want stricter SLOs for SIEM ingestion on Dedicated customers? (ops + sales impact assessment required)

End of playbook.
